title: The Snow That Would Not Fall

npcs.name: Aud
npcs.about: The last keeper of the monastery. Swept the floor around the Shaper's body for nine winters.

npcs.name: Old Maren
npcs.about: Leads the pilgrims. Remembers snow that fell.

npcs.name: Tobin
npcs.about: A pilgrim child who follows things.

npcs.name: Isolde
npcs.about: Keeps the camp's lantern. Plays the lyre at night.

npcs.name: Varo
npcs.about: A staff-bearer who walked out to watch the Warden and did not come back.

aud.wake.speaker: aud
lines: You stood up out of his robe.
Nine winters I swept around him. I thought the cloth would rot before it moved.
The snow on the steppe has not fallen since he died. It hangs. Go down and see it.
There is a shrine below the cliffs. The stones there still remember him.

aud.again.speaker: aud
lines: Down. The shrine, then the pilgrims' fire.

aud.after.speaker: aud
lines: I heard the wind on the bell this morning. I had forgotten the note it makes.

maren.first.speaker: maren
lines: A robe with no one in it. The stories said you would come like this.
Out past the stone, something old lies across the steppe and holds the snow in the air.
Varo went to watch it. He has not come back to the fire.
And the boy has wandered again. If you see small tracks, follow them.

maren.again.speaker: maren
lines: Varo is at the watching stone, east. Go quietly. It sleeps lightly.

maren.tobin.speaker: maren
lines: You brought him back. Take this. It was a Shaper's, before it was ours.

maren.night.speaker: maren
lines: My mother saw them once. Tall, robed like you. They walked ahead of the weather.
Where they stopped, the snow came down. Where they went on, it followed.

maren.after.speaker: maren
lines: Listen. Snow is falling on the tents. I am too old to cry about weather, and I am crying about weather.

tobin.found.speaker: tobin
lines: There's water under the ice. It's not moving either.
I'm not lost. I was following the quiet.

options.text: Let him listen a while longer.

tobin.again.speaker: tobin
lines: Do you have a face in there? Maren says no. I think it's just dark.

tobin.after.speaker: tobin
lines: The spring is talking now. It doesn't say anything. It just talks.

isolde.day.speaker: isolde
lines: The lantern was lit at the monastery. I carry it so the fire never has to start from nothing.

isolde.night.speaker: isolde
lines: Sit, if you sit. I only know the slow songs. The fast ones need wind.

isolde.after.speaker: isolde
lines: The flame leans now. I had never seen it lean.

varo.first.speaker: varo
lines: There. Do you see it? I thought it was a ridge for three days.
It breathes once an hour. Its knees are water, held still.
Freeze what moves in it, and break what you freeze. Then let it lie down.

varo.again.speaker: varo
lines: Its knees. Then its hips. Do not stand where it is looking.

varo.after.speaker: varo
lines: It is a hill now. A good hill. I will tell them it lay down on its own; they would not believe the rest.
Far off, the first snow in nine winters reaches the ground.

quests.title: The Empty Robe
quests.summary: Something has woken in the last Shaper's robe.

steps.journal: I woke in the monastery where the last Shaper died. A keeper named Aud was waiting.
Aud told me of a shrine below the cliffs whose stones remember the Shaper.
Pilgrims keep a fire on the plain below. They may know why the snow hangs.

quests.title: The Held Snow
quests.summary: A Warden lies across the steppe, holding its snow in the air.

steps.journal: Maren says Varo went east to watch the Warden. He waits at the watching stone.
Varo: its knees are water, held still. Freeze them, break them, and let it lie down.

quests.title: First Snow
quests.summary: The Warden has lain down. Motion is returning to the steppe.

steps.journal: The snow is falling again. The pilgrims should see it.
Snow on the tents. Maren is waiting by the fire.

quests.title: A Trail in the Snow
quests.summary: A pilgrim child has wandered from the fire.

steps.journal: Small footprints lead west from the pilgrims' fire.
I found Tobin at a frozen spring, listening to it. Maren will want him back.

quests.title: The Sleeping Spring
quests.summary: Water lies still under the ice west of the camp.

steps.journal: Tobin said the water under the ice isn't moving. Perhaps it needs to be held harder before it can let go.
I froze the spring solid. When the steppe is released, it may run.

quests.title: The Stones Remember
quests.summary: Five shrines stand on the frost steppe. Each remembers a Shaper's step.

steps.journal: Shrines on the steppe: the stones are warm under the frost. Find all five.

quests.title: The Slow Songs
quests.summary: Isolde plays at night by the pilgrims' fire.

steps.journal: Isolde only knows the slow songs. She plays them at night.

echo-frost-hold.name: Echo of the Held Breath
echo-frost-hold.effect: Frozen joints and Shaped stay frozen 40% longer.
echo-frost-hold.text: What is held may be held a little longer.

echo-frost-surf.name: Echo of the Running Water
echo-frost-surf.effect: Snow-surf keeps its speed longer on flats.
echo-frost-surf.text: Water remembers which way is down.

echo-frost-still.name: Echo of the Still Stone
echo-frost-still.effect: Focus returns faster while standing still.
echo-frost-still.text: The stones were patient. So were they.

lore-shapers-walked.title: They Walked Ahead of the Weather
lore-shapers-walked.text: The Shapers did not command the snow. They walked, and the snow came after, the way a dog follows someone it loves. — as told by Old Maren

lore-spring.title: The Sleeping Spring
lore-spring.text: Beneath the ice the water stands in the shape it had when the last Shaper died, mid-ripple, waiting to finish the motion.

lore-five-stones.title: The Five Stones
lore-five-stones.text: Each shrine marks where a Shaper stood still for a night. It was the only stillness they allowed themselves. The stones kept it for them.

lore-slow-songs.title: The Slow Songs
lore-slow-songs.text: Pilgrims' songs lost their quick verses as the wind died. Isolde says the quick verses were about weather, and no one could remember what weather sounded like.
